sentences.text: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest.-(1) Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on an accusation of having committed a non- bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction under this section that in the event of such arrest, he shall be released on bail; and
sentences._hearing_file: Paramjit Kaur vs State Of Punjab on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
that court may, after taking into consideration, inter alia, the following 3 of 5 Neutral Citation No:= CRM-M-727-2023 (O&M) -4- factors, namely:- (i) The nature and gravity of the accusation;
(ii) The antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a court in respect of any cognizable offence; (iii) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; and (iv)
where the accusation has been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by having him so arrested, either reject the application forthwith or issue an interim order for the grant of anticipatory bail."
8.

sentences.text: In view of the above, it is mandatory on the part of the court to ensure the compliance of the pre-requisite conditions for grant of anticipatory bail including the nature and gravity of the accusation.

sentences.text: There is no substantial difference between Sections 438 and 439 Cr.P.C. so far as appreciation of the case as to whether or not a bail is to be granted, is concerned.

sentences.text: However, neither anticipatory bail nor regular bail can be granted as a matter of rule.
sentences._hearing_file: Paramjit Kaur vs State Of Punjab on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The anticipatory bail being an extraordinary privilege should be granted only in exceptional cases.

sentences.text: The judicial discretion conferred upon the court has to be properly exercised after proper application of mind to decide whether it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: The High Court ought to have exercised its extraordinary jurisdiction following the parameters laid down by this Court in above referred to judicial pronouncements, considering the nature and gravity of the offence and as the FIR had been lodged spontaneously, its veracity is reliable.

A complaint was filed by petitioner Ram Kishan to the SSP Pathankot on 03.08.2022 that the complainant has taken money from him.
He has also produced the photographs showing that he is doing marketing of the said Crypto Currency alluring people to invest in Crypto Currencies through companies like Gulf Coin etc.
The other FIR under Section 420 is registered against the petitioner.
Custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required.
